headline.purpose: A page title; there is no display size.

nav.purpose: Nav rail and floating panel labels.

label.purpose: What a readout or group is; words, not caps.

caption.purpose: Units, source lines, metadata; the most used size.

readout-id.purpose: The robot id in the status strip.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: A command: the one action a screen or dialog commits.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:6px; height:32px; padding:0 10px; border-radius:4px; border:1px solid transparent; font-family: var(--font-mona-sans, 'Mona Sans'), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size:14px; font-weight:500; white-space:nowrap; cursor:pointer; transition: background-color .15s, color .15s, border-color .15s; background:var(--signal-cmd, #0a6d94); color:#fff; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--signal-cmd, #0a6d94) 80%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--signal-cmd, #0a6d94); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: A secondary action beside a primary one.

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: Delete or discard: red text on a tint, never a solid red.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:6px; height:32px; padding:0 10px; border-radius:4px; border:1px solid transparent; font-family: var(--font-mona-sans, 'Mona Sans'), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size:14px; font-weight:500; white-space:nowrap; cursor:pointer; transition: background-color .15s, color .15s, border-color .15s; background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--signal-warn, #c02f34) 10%, transparent); color:var(--signal-warn, #c02f34); } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--signal-warn, #c02f34) 20%, transparent); } .ds-btn-destructive:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--signal-cmd, #0a6d94); outline-offset: 2px; outline-color:var(--signal-warn, #c02f34); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: A field: hairline stroke, cyan on focus.

components.name: Tone Chip
components.description: A status in its signal hue: tinted, hairline in the hue.

components.name: Emergency Stop
components.description: First press on every screen: engages at pointer-down, releases on a one-second hold.
components.css: .ds-estop { position:relative; display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; width:56px; height:56px; overflow:hidden; border:1px solid transparent; border-radius:2.4px; background:transparent; color:var(--signal-warn, #c02f34); cursor:pointer; transition: background-color .15s, color .15s, border-color .15s; } .ds-estop svg { position:relative; } .ds-estop:hover { border-color:var(--signal-warn, #c02f34); background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--signal-warn, #c02f34) 12%, transparent); color:var(--signal-warn, #c02f34); } .ds-estop:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--signal-cmd, #0a6d94); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-estop-engaged { border-color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--signal-warn, #c02f34) 50%, transparent); background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--signal-warn, #c02f34) 12%, transparent); color:var(--signal-warn, #c02f34); } .ds-estop-hold { position:absolute; inset:0 auto 0 0; width:0; background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--signal-warn, #c02f34) 30%, transparent); transition: width 1000ms linear; } .ds-estop-engaged:active .ds-estop-hold { width:100%; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-estop-hold { transition:none; } }

narrative.overview:
The console borrows an aircraft EFIS's colour semantics because they map onto a
navigation stack almost one to one. Colour is never decoration here: five
signal hues each name what a value *is* (measured, commanded, active guidance,
degraded, faulted), and they mean the same thing in the chrome as on the 3D
map. Everything else is a cool, quiet neutral ground that lets those five read
at a glance. The operator reads this screen the way a pilot reads a panel:
in short looks, often while the machine is moving.

Density is instrument-grade. Readouts are rows, not cards: a caption label,
a hairline and a tabular number, with the frame spending as few pixels as
possible. Surfaces are rectilinear, nearly square-cornered and flat, separated
by tone and hairlines rather than shadows. The 3D viewport is the recessed
"well" every panel sits around. Day and night are both first-class themes:
day is cool paper for an operator in a lit site or outdoors, night is hull
graphite for a dim one. Neither is the default the other was derived from.

Motion is functional and scarce: a sweep across the status strip once per
telemetry frame (proof the link is alive), a hold bar filling on the stop's
release, a climbing battery meter while charging. Every one of them stops
under reduced motion.
keyCharacteristics: Five EFIS signal hues carry all meaning; neutrals carry everything else.
One sans (Mona Sans) for words, one mono (JetBrains Mono, tabular) for every measured quantity.
Corners of 4 px at most on anything rectangular; pills are the only round shape.
Flat: tone steps and 1 px hairlines separate surfaces; shadows only lift overlays and things being dragged.
Day and night are equal themes, switched from the nav rail's foot.
Touch targets grow to 40 px under a coarse pointer, by CSS, at any width.

rules.name: The Meaning-First Rule
rules.body: Pick a hue by what the value *is* (measured, commanded, active, degraded, faulted), never by how it looks. A green that does not mean "measured and valid" is a bug.

rules.name: The One Language Rule
rules.body: Chrome and canvas share the same five hues. A token moved in `app/globals.css` is moved in `lib/theme/signal.ts` in the same change, because a canvas cannot read a CSS variable.

rules.name: The Ramp Is Not A Signal Rule
rules.body: The height ramp never stands in for a signal, and no signal hue is used to colour heights: a floor two storeys up must not read as a command or a fault.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every measured quantity is set in the readout face with tabular figures. A number that reflows as its digits change cannot be read at a glance, which is the only way this screen is read.

rules.name: The No-Caps Rule
rules.body: Labels are words in the sans at caption size, not condensed uppercase. Size and colour separate "what this is" from "what it says". Job ids are never uppercased: an uppercased id is a different string from the one an engineer greps for.

rules.name: The One Markup Rule
rules.body: A row that must become two rows wraps; it is never rendered twice behind `hidden` / `sm:hidden`.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: A surface that sits in the layout — floating map panels included — never casts a shadow; only an overlay or something in the hand may.

rules.name: The Ring-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Keyboard focus is a 2 px outline in Commanded Cyan, offset 2 px, never a shadow — a shadow is swallowed by the 3D canvas behind it.

rules.name: The Four-Pixel Rule
rules.body: No rectangular surface rounds past 4 px. A soft, bubbly corner reads as a consumer app, not an instrument.

dos: **Do** choose a signal hue by what the value is, and use the same hue for it in the chrome and on the 3D map.
**Do** set every number in the readout face with tabular figures.
**Do** keep rectangular corners at 4 px or less and separate surfaces with tone and 1 px hairlines.
**Do** design both themes; check the day theme in particular, since outdoor operators depend on it.
**Do** give every state words: an empty, loading, failed or unknown readout says so (`No task message in queue`, `Job list unavailable`), never a blank.
**Do** grow targets to 40 px with `pointer-coarse:` and input text to 16 px, in CSS.
donts: **Don't** use a signal hue for decoration, branding or emphasis — a hue with no meaning dilutes the five that have one.
**Don't** wrap a few readouts in a card; use an instrument group.
**Don't** make a destructive button solid red, or use a shadow on a surface that sits in the layout.
**Don't** set labels in condensed uppercase, or uppercase a job id.
**Don't** add a hand-written `matchMedia` hook or render a row twice for phone and desktop.
**Don't** use `window.confirm`; a delete is asked through the confirm dialog (Keep / Delete).
**Don't** colour heights with signal hues or signals with the height ramp.
